candidates.comment: A translation of work relation between a creative work and the original work from which it was translated. Also called original work, source work, translated from. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Don Quixote (Spanish)' translationOfWork 'Don Quijote (original)'", "CreativeWork 'The Little Prince (English)' translationOfWork 'Le Petit Prince (French)'", "CreativeWork 'War and Peace (English)' translationOfWork 'Война и мир (Russian)'".

candidates.label: workHours
candidates.comment: A work hours relation between a job posting and a text description, specifying the typical schedule or shifts for the position. Also called working schedule, shift pattern, typical hours. Examples: JobPosting workHours "9am-5pm, Mon-Fri", JobPosting workHours "Night Shift", JobPosting workHours "Flexible".

candidates.label: encodesCreativeWork
candidates.comment: An encodes creative work relation between a media object and the creative work it represents or contains. Also called "represents work", "contains work", "media of work". Examples: "Video file encodesCreativeWork 'Movie Title'", "Audio recording encodesCreativeWork 'Song Title'", "Image file encodesCreativeWork 'Painting Title'". Distinct from encoding, which is the inverse relation (CreativeWork -> MediaObject).

instances: Elizabeth Dunford -> University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
Marissa Burgermaster -> University of Texas at Austin
Jane Houlihan -> Healthy Babies Bright Futures

candidates.label: affiliation
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a person and an organization they are associated with. Also called associated with, member of, works for, belongs to. Examples: "A professor's affiliation is 'Harvard University'.", "A player's affiliation is 'Local Soccer Club'." Distinct from alumniOf, which specifies a past association with an educational organization.

candidates.label: hospitalAffiliation
candidates.comment: A hospital affiliation relation between a physician and a hospital they are affiliated with. Also called affiliated hospital, associated hospital, hospital connection. Examples: "A physician has a hospital affiliation with 'General Hospital'.", "The doctor's hospital affiliation is a major medical center.", "This physician is affiliated with a specific hospital."

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: practicesAt
candidates.comment: A professional affiliation relation between an individual physician and the medical organization where they practice. Also called works at, affiliated with, employed by, is a doctor at. Examples: Dr. Smith practices at 'General Hospital'. Dr. Jones practices at 'City Clinic'. The physician practices at 'Family Health Center'.

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.

candidates.label: program
candidates.comment: An association between a program membership and the specific member program it belongs to. Also called part of program, associated program, membership program. Examples: "A loyalty card membership is part of the 'Star Alliance Gold' program.", "A gym membership is part of the 'Premium Fitness' program.", "A frequent flyer membership is part of the 'SkyMiles' program.". Distinct from programName, which is the textual name of the program.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

chosen_property.label: proposedRuleIn
chosen_property.definition: The government organization proposed a rule in a specific year.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation.

candidates.label: suggestedAnswer
candidates.comment: A proposed response or set of responses to a question. Also called "possible answer", "proposed solution", "answer option", "response to question". Examples: "The question has suggestedAnswer 'Yes'", "The quiz question's suggestedAnswer is a multiple-choice list", "This question provides a suggestedAnswer for users."

candidates.label: suggestedMeasurement
candidates.comment: A quantitative value representing a suggested range of body measurements for an intended audience or person, often for wearable products. Also called "size recommendation", "body measurement range", "fit guide", "sizing suggestion". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedMeasurement inseam 32-34 inches", "The size specification includes suggestedMeasurement height 170-190 cm", "This product is designed for a suggestedMeasurement chest 40-42 inches."

candidates.label: suggestedMaxAge
candidates.comment: A numerical value indicating the maximum recommended age in years for an audience or user. Also called "maximum age", "upper age limit", "age cap". Examples: "The game has suggestedMaxAge 12", "The audience specification includes suggestedMaxAge 65", "This content is suitable up to suggestedMaxAge 18.". Distinct from suggestedAge, which specifies a range, and suggestedMinAge, which specifies only the minimum.

candidates.label: suggestedMinAge
candidates.comment: A numerical value indicating the minimum recommended age in years for an audience or user. Also called "minimum age", "lower age limit", "age floor". Examples: "The game has suggestedMinAge 7", "The audience specification includes suggestedMinAge 18", "This content is suitable from suggestedMinAge 3.". Distinct from suggestedAge, which specifies a range, and suggestedMaxAge, which specifies only the maximum.

candidates.label: suggestedAge
candidates.comment: A quantitative value indicating the recommended age or age range for an intended audience or person. Also called "recommended age", "age range", "target age", "suitable age". Examples: "The toy has suggestedAge 3-5 years", "The audience specification includes suggestedAge 18+", "This product is for suggestedAge 6-12 months.". Distinct from suggestedMinAge and suggestedMaxAge, which specify only the minimum or maximum.

candidates.label: permittedUsage
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the allowed uses or activities within an accommodation. Also called allowed uses, usage rules, permitted activities. Examples: An apartment has a permitted usage of 'Residential Only'. A hotel room has a permitted usage of 'Short-term Stay'. A conference hall has a permitted usage of 'Events and Meetings'.

candidates.label: boardingPolicy
candidates.comment: A type of boarding policy used by an airline or for a flight. Also called: boarding procedure, airline boarding rules. Examples: "Airline 'United' boardingPolicy 'BoardingPolicyType.ZoneBoarding'", "Flight 'Flight 789' boardingPolicy 'Group-based boarding'."

candidates.label: suggestedGender
candidates.comment: An indication of the recommended gender for an intended person or audience. Also called "target gender", "audience gender", "gender recommendation". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedGender unisex", "The audience specification includes suggestedGender female", "This product is for suggestedGender male."

candidates.label: recommendedIntake
candidates.comment: A recommended intake relation between a dietary supplement and the suggested dosage schedule for a specific population. Also called suggested dosage, dosage instructions, intake guidelines. Examples: "A vitamin supplement has a recommended intake '1 tablet daily for adults'.", "A mineral supplement has a recommended intake '2 capsules twice a day'.", "A protein powder has a recommended intake '30g post-workout'."

candidates.label: healthPlanCoinsuranceOption
candidates.comment: A coinsurance option relation between a health plan cost-sharing specification and a description of how coinsurance applies. Also called coinsurance rule, coinsurance terms, option for coinsurance. Examples: "Health plan cost-sharing has a coinsurance option 'after deductible'.", "The specification includes a coinsurance option.", "This plan's coinsurance option is 'before deductible'."

candidates.label: item
candidates.comment: A list element relation between a data feed item or list item and the entity it represents within a collection. Also called represents, refers to, entry, element. Examples: A list item has an item of 'John Doe'. A data feed item has an item of 'Product X'. A list entry has an item of 'Event Y'.

candidates.label: hasRepresentation
candidates.comment: A representation relation between a biochemical entity and its common symbolic or structural representation. Also called represented by, symbolic form, structural representation. Examples: "A BioChemEntity has a representation as a chemical structure.", "The entity has a representation as a text sequence.", "This biochemical entity has a URL representation."

candidates.label: encoding
candidates.comment: An encoding relation between a creative work and a media object that represents or contains it. Also called "represented by media", "media representation", "has media object". Examples: "Movie 'The Matrix' encoding 'Matrix.mp4'", "Song 'Bohemian Rhapsody' encoding 'BohemianRhapsody.mp3'", "Book '1984' encoding '1984.epub'". Distinct from encodesCreativeWork, which is the inverse relation (MediaObject -> CreativeWork).

candidates.label: encodings
candidates.comment: An encodings relation between a creative work and the media objects that represent or contain it. Also called "represented by media objects", "has media representations", "media versions". Examples: "Movie 'The Matrix' encodings 'Matrix.mp4', 'Matrix.avi'", "Song 'Bohemian Rhapsody' encodings 'BohemianRhapsody.mp3', 'BohemianRhapsody.wav'", "Book '1984' encodings '1984.epub', '1984.pdf'". Distinct from encodesCreativeWork, which is the inverse relation (MediaObject -> CreativeWork).

candidates.label: encodesCreativeWork
candidates.comment: An encodes creative work relation between a media object and the creative work it represents or contains. Also called "represents work", "contains work", "media of work". Examples: "Video file encodesCreativeWork 'Movie Title'", "Audio recording encodesCreativeWork 'Song Title'", "Image file encodesCreativeWork 'Painting Title'". Distinct from encoding, which is the inverse relation (CreativeWork -> MediaObject).

candidates.label: representativeOfPage
candidates.comment: A representative of page relation indicating whether an image object accurately reflects the content of the web page it appears on. Also called page representative, content summary image. Examples: "A thumbnail image is representative of page 'true'.", "A decorative image is representative of page 'false'.", "A product photo is representative of page 'true'."

candidates.label: tickerSymbol
candidates.comment: A textual identifier representing the exchange-traded instrument associated with a corporation, typically an exchange and instrument name. Also called "stock symbol", "stock ticker", "exchange symbol", "trading symbol". Examples: "Apple Inc. has tickerSymbol NASDAQ AAPL", "The corporation's tickerSymbol is NYSE GOOG", "This company is identified by its tickerSymbol."

candidates.label: nationality
candidates.comment: A country representing the nationality of a person. Also called citizenship, country of origin, national identity. Examples: "Person A nationality 'United States'", "Person B nationality 'France'", "Person C nationality 'Japan'". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the location where a person was born.

candidates.label: logo
candidates.comment: A logo relation between a brand, certification, organization, place, product, or service and its associated image or URL. Also called: brand logo, official emblem, corporate identity. Examples: "Apple Inc. logo Apple Logo Image", "Nike Product logo Nike Swoosh", "Olympic Games logo Olympic Rings".

candidates.label: photo
candidates.comment: A visual attribute linking a place to a single photograph depicting it. Also called image, picture, visual representation. Examples: A restaurant has a photo of its interior. A park has a photo of its main entrance. A landmark has a photo of its facade. Distinct from photos, which links to multiple photographs.

chosen_property.label: analyzedDataIn
chosen_property.definition: The person analyzed data in a specific city.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation.

candidates.label: measurementTechnique
candidates.comment: A measurement technique relation between a data catalog, data download, dataset, observation, property value, or statistical variable and the technique, method, or technology used for measurement. Also called: measurement approach, data collection method, analytical technique. Examples: "Molecule Concentration Dataset measurementTechnique 'Mass Spectrometry'", "Depression Rating Observation measurementTechnique 'Beck Depression Inventory'", "Water Quality Data measurementTechnique 'Chromatography'". Distinct from measurementMethod, which is a more specific subproperty.

candidates.label: data
candidates.comment: An association relation between an instantaneous event and the data linked to it. Also called: event data, associated data, event information. Examples: "Sensor Reading Event" data "temperature: 25C, humidity: 60%", "Log Entry Event" data "User 'admin' logged in from IP 192.168.1.1", "System Alert Event" data "Error code 500: Database connection failed".

candidates.label: variableMeasured
candidates.comment: A variable measured relation between a dataset or observation and the variables that are measured within it. Also called measured variable, data variable, observation parameter. Examples: "Dataset variableMeasured 'Temperature'", "Observation variableMeasured 'Humidity'", "Dataset variableMeasured 'Patient Age'".

candidates.label: dataset
candidates.comment: A containment relation between a data catalog and a dataset included within it. Also called: cataloged dataset, included dataset, data collection. Examples: "Government Data Catalog" dataset "Population Census 2020", "Research Data Repository" dataset "Climate Change Projections", "Open Data Portal" dataset "Public Transport Schedules".

candidates.label: datasetTimeInterval
candidates.comment: A temporal applicability relation between a dataset and its relevant time range. Also called: dataset time range, temporal coverage, data period. Examples: "Census Data" dataset time interval "2011", "Historical Weather Data" dataset time interval "1950-2000", "Economic Survey" dataset time interval "2022-01-01/2022-12-31".

candidates.label: diseaseSpreadStatistics
candidates.comment: A disease spread statistics relation between a special announcement and a dataset, observation, URL, or web content containing statistical information about the spread of a disease. Also called "epidemic data", "infection rates", "case statistics". Examples: "Special announcement diseaseSpreadStatistics 'Dataset of daily cases'", "Public health update diseaseSpreadStatistics 'WebContent on regional spread'", "COVID-19 alert diseaseSpreadStatistics 'URL to dashboard'".

candidates.label: healthcareReportingData
candidates.comment: A healthcare reporting data relation between a hospital and its associated reporting data, such as CDC records or datasets. Also called hospital data, reporting dataset, healthcare metrics. Examples: "A hospital has healthcare reporting data from the CDC.", "The hospital provides healthcare reporting data as a dataset.", "This facility publishes its healthcare reporting data."

candidates.label: study
candidates.comment: A relation between a medical entity and a medical study or trial that investigates it. Also called "related study", "investigated by study", "medical trial". Examples: "The drug has study a clinical trial", "The medical condition is part of a study", "This therapy is being evaluated in a study."

candidates.label: includedInDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included in data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included in data catalog."

candidates.label: includedDataCatalog
candidates.comment: A data catalog inclusion relation between a dataset and the data catalog that contains it. Also called part of catalog, contained in catalog, catalog member. Examples: "A dataset is included in a data catalog.", "The data is part of an included data catalog.", "This dataset belongs to a specific included data catalog."

instances: American Academy of Pediatrics -> Ultraprocessed Food Prevalence

chosen_property.label: statesFact
chosen_property.definition: The professional organization states that a particular nutrition fact is true.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation.

candidates.label: orderStatus
candidates.comment: The current status of an entire order. Also called order state, transaction status, fulfillment state. Examples: "Order 123 orderStatus 'OrderProcessing'", "Order 456 orderStatus 'OrderDelivered'", "Order 789 orderStatus 'OrderCancelled'". Distinct from orderItemStatus, which is for individual items within an order.

candidates.label: addressRegion
candidates.comment: An address region relation between a defined region or postal address and the administrative division (e.g., state, province) it belongs to. Also called state, province, administrative area. Examples: "A postal address's address region is 'CA'.", "The address region is 'Bavaria'."

candidates.label: nationality
candidates.comment: A country representing the nationality of a person. Also called citizenship, country of origin, national identity. Examples: "Person A nationality 'United States'", "Person B nationality 'France'", "Person C nationality 'Japan'". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the location where a person was born.

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: validIn
candidates.comment: A valid in relation between a certification, credential, or permit and the geographic area where it is valid. Also called valid region, applicable area, geographic validity. Examples: "Permit validIn 'California'", "Certification validIn 'European Union'", "Credential validIn 'United States'".

candidates.label: status
candidates.comment: An indication of the current state or status of a medical condition, procedure, or study. Also called "current state", "condition status", "study progress", "procedure status". Examples: "The medical study has status Recruiting", "The patient's condition status is stable", "The procedure's status is completed."

candidates.label: actionStatus
candidates.comment: An action status relation between an action and its current disposition or state. Also called action state, status of action, disposition. Examples: "A 'purchase' action's action status is 'CompletedActionStatus'.", "A 'shipment' action's action status is 'PotentialActionStatus'."

candidates.label: reservationStatus
candidates.comment: A reservation status relation between a reservation and its current state, such as confirmed or cancelled. Also called booking status, status of reservation. Examples: "A flight reservation has a reservation status 'Confirmed'.", "A hotel booking has a reservation status 'Pending'.", "A restaurant reservation has a reservation status 'Cancelled'."

candidates.label: returnPolicyCountry
candidates.comment: The country designated as the destination for product returns under a merchant return policy. Also called return destination country, country for returns, return shipping country. Examples: `US Return Policy` returnPolicyCountry `"US"`, `European Return Policy` returnPolicyCountry `Country: Germany`, `International Return Policy` returnPolicyCountry `"CA"`.

candidates.label: serverStatus
candidates.comment: The current operational status of a game server. Also called server state, game server condition, operational status. Examples: `Game Server A` serverStatus `Online`, `Game Server B` serverStatus `Offline`, `Game Server C` serverStatus `Maintenance`.
